It tends to be stronger to have a few Star-spending cards which generate great output from your Stars than the throw tons of them into your deck, which results in Stars being spent on unupgraded cards with less output.

~Free win with Clone, which is cool, just make sure you have a potion/relic for the rare fights which counter it, like the Insects who only take 9 per hit!

GLOW.text: Goes into decks with extra Energy and need for Star generation, but not a great pickup in Act 1 usually due to its low output, and not necessarily appealing later in the run either.

PHOTON_CUT.text: Somewhat more exciting when paired with Kingly cards which care about being drawn multiple times, or if you can find an upgraded one, but for the most part this is outshone by Regent's other commons.

SOLAR_STRIKE.text: So-so Common. A bit of output, but nothing exceptional.

SPOILS_OF_BATTLE.text: Regent's best Common card draw which doesn't require Stars, so Spoils will pull some weight in high-energy runs sometimes, but not a good card in Act 1 by default.

ALIGNMENT.text: Alignment doesn't usually have much purpose in Regent's card pool unless you're using it for an infinite or massive X-cost card. You typically have to spend energy to generate Stars, if you're just using them to create energy again you start getting Rube Goldberg-y and failing to actually output anything that wins fights.

CONVERGENCE.text: Retaining your Hand is occasionally strong in runs which want to line certain cards up with each other, but Convergence has very limited output other than that Retain, so don't try to force it into a deck which doesn't benefit from it much.

GLIMMER.text: Passable card draw, but only exceptional when paired with a deck which benefits from putting a card on top of its Draw Pile. Otherwise, there are Common draw options which outperform this.

HEGEMONY.text: Regent doesn't have a ton of ways to benefit from a turn with extra Energy, and Hegemony is a lot of Energy to spend on not much Output.

KNOCKOUT_BLOW.text: Lots of things have to go right for this to be meaningfully better than a card which deals 30 Damage for 3 Energy, but 30 Damage for 3 Energy is enough to make it into the deck every now and then.

ORBIT.text: Decent Energy generation over time, if your deck needs that.

QUASAR.text: Colorless Cards are quite powerful, but 2 Star cost and the fact you'll still have to pay the Energy to play the Colorless card makes Quasar a bit of a tough sell for me.

TERRAFORMING.text: Good Support card, at its best when paired with very specifically Stardust or Radiate.

BUNDLE_OF_JOY.text: Solid if you have cards which reward you for generating cards, but otherwise quite slow and unreliable.

NEUTRON_AEGIS.text: 8+ Plating is great, but 5 Stars is a huge amount to pay. I'd find this card stronger if it costs 3 Energy, at which point it could go into any deck severely lacking Block, but here it really only fits into a deck severely lacking Block which ALSO generates a good number of Stars.

DEFEND_REGENT.text: Regent does need to play Defends at the start of the run to avoid dying, but can quickly replace them with better Block options.

DEVASTATE.text: Great to generate off of an Attack potion, but 4 Stars is a very awkward cost for early in the game, and Devastate doesn't really deal much more damage than some of Regent's more straightforward Commons, while failing to scale impressively with any of his main synergy spaces.

FURNACE.text: Passable damage for a Boss fight if your deck is lacking a way to scale up, but otherwise very slow.

MONOLOGUE.text: There are ways to make Monologue particularly strong, but it's hard to find any that are more impressive than making Vigor instead.

PROPHESIZE.text: Extremely difficult to find spots where you have so much Energy that you want to spend 2 to draw 6 cards, but if you ever do, Prophesize is available.

FOREGONE_CONCLUSION.text: Very slow, and no guarantee it can actually get you the cards you need, as it can't search your Discard Pile.

MONARCHS_GAZE.text: An expensive card, although it has a strong effect. Best off a Power Potion in a Boss Fight, but occasionally can make it into your deck if you lack Block and have ways to hit enemies multiple times per turn.

ROYALTIES.text: If you successfully survive 5 fights drawing and playing Royalties you'll probably have made enough Gold using it to successfully remove it from your deck.

BONE_SHARDS.text: Extremely high numbers for a 1-Cost card, and in the toughest fights in the game you'll often be piloting a deck where Osty only has 1 or 2 Hitpoints when you sacrifice him anyway.

BORROWED_TIME.text:
In a hand of 1-Cost cards Borrowed Time already lets you play one extra card this turn, but it's at its best with X-Cost cards (which don't have their cost effected by it at all!) or higher cost cards and their synergies (it makes all 1-Costs 2-Costs instead, for cards which care about that!).

Tons of energy, good upgrade, and doesn't have exhaust, so can be used multiple times in some fights.

DANSE_MACABRE.text: Massive payoff card for one of Necrobinder's best synergy spaces. Especially powerful when paired with Borrowed Time, another of Necrobinder's best cards. Increasing your Block output per turn is one of the simpler shortcuts toward winning a run of Slay the Spire 2.

SLEIGHT_OF_FLESH.text: Around 20-25% of Necrobinder's cards apply debuffs, and 9(13) damage is a lot of damage to attach to them. Keep in mind that Doom counts as a debuff!

DEMESNE.text: Extremely powerful effect, well-worth spending 2 or 3 energy on for longer fights, and fine to treat as an Ethereal Curse in shorter ones. Typically a card you'll take later in a run to shore up your Boss Matchups.

END_OF_DAYS.text: Stand-out card for several of the fastest fights in the game. Not particularly impressive in longer fights, but can still be passable in them.

ERADICATE.text: Prime enchant target, excellent payoff for many of Necrobinder's stronger scaling support cards (especially Lethality, Borrowed Time, and Transfigure). There are a surprisingly large number of different things in the game which can make this card one-shot the final boss.

NEUROSURGE.text: Necrobinder's best card. Keep in mind that there are even ways to make applying Doom every turn an upside!

TRANSFIGURE.text: Especially good with X cards, which won't actually have their energy cost modified and will play for the same amount twice. Flexible way to increase the output of the cards in your hand right now, which can double as a way to combo with specific cards in your deck in longer fights to win against tougher enemies.

GLIMPSE_BEYOND.text: Extremely strong card draw option for multiplayer.

BLIGHT_STRIKE.text: Excellent damage for 1 energy, and scales well with both Doom and Debuff synergy later in the run. Worth picking to win the tougher Act 1 fights, and often retains some value as the run progresses.

DEFY.text: Lots of block for a 1-Cost Common, and some other cards can reward you for having Ethereal cards in your deck, so it's nice to take one or two which are above par early on in the game in case you see them.

INVOKE.text:
In decks with good card draw or high Energy costs, one or more Invokes can feel great to play. Necrobinder can build some very high energy decks, so having one Invoke to play per turn can sometimes feel extremely strong.

I don't hate taking one of these in Act 1, but tend to wait until I have something appealing to actually spend the energy on.

PULL_AGGRO.text: Being able to spend two Energy on Block semi-efficiently is a nice thing to get out of a Common, and Necrobinder also has some synergies with higher cost cards which this taps into later in the run. Often happy to take one in Act 1 and will sometimes take more later.

SCOURGE.text: Excellent damage for Act 1, and card draw is a powerful thing to have in your deck for later in the game. Decent upgrade.

SNAP.text:
Retain is an extremely powerful keyword, and keep in mind that Snap applies it to a card until the end of a fight, not just this turn.

Almost always happy to have one of these in my deck, and it's nice that it deals a little damage for fights as well.

CAPTURE_SPIRIT.text: All told, an unupgraded Capture Spirit draws you a net +2 cards over the course of however long it takes you to draw and play the Souls it creates, which is fine. It's best in decks with high velocity, so they can benefit from the Souls faster, extra energy to take advantage of the extra cards, or Soul synergies. It'll often be good by the end of the run!

DEATHS_DOOR.text: 18 Block for 1 Energy, scaling three times with any Dexterity you have, is extremely powerful. Death's Door is one of the main reasons to be excited about dealing damage via Doom.

DEATHBRINGER.text: Slow, but extremely high numbers, and good for both damage and defense. A lot of decks are happy to have this card.

DEBILITATE.text: Doubling the effect of Weak on threatening enemies is extremely powerful, without even considering that this card deals decent damage for 1, works with Vulnerable as well, and counts as applying a debuff of its own.

DELAY.text: Nice to be able to sink energy into defense on a turn, and Delay also sets you up for a big turn next turn. Good upgrade, increasing the energy gain to two, as well.

DIRGE.text: Only a passable card in an unsupported situation, but when paired with energy gain or other synergies Dirge can create a massive payoff. Usually okay with taking one in Act 1, but most excited to add it in a deck which already has strong support for it.

ENFEEBLING_TOUCH.text: Good ethereal synergy piece, and excellent defensive card for many of the most threatening turns in the game.

FETCH.text: There's very little downside to taking a Fetch, and there are occasionally extra upsides to having an extra attack to play on a turn beyond just the 3 damage.

FRIENDSHIP.text: Necrobinder can often deal damage without caring about Strength, and gaining an extra energy per turn for the rest of the fight unlocks a lot of potential later in the run. Don't overdo it with multiple copies in a deck which doesn't even need the extra energy though, as it's a little slow.

LETHALITY.text: Excellent damage increase for any deck playing high damage Attacks. If that's what your deck is doing, it's somewhat difficult to ever have too many copies of Lethality.

NO_ESCAPE.text: Bigtime payoff card for decks relying on Doom for longer fights, but don't overestimate it in a run where you don't have Doom damage already. Also keep in mind that you need to apply a substantial amount of Doom before this is doing much better than a damage Common.

PARSE.text: Ethereal synergies and card draw. Nothing special in Act 1 because you don't have much to draw with it yet, and don't have extra energy to spend yet, but as the run goes on Parse typically gets better and better.

PULL_FROM_BELOW.text: Massive payoff card for longer fights in decks with a few Ethereal cards. Strong enough to consider speculating on even if you've only gotten one or two Ethereal cards so far.

PUTREFY.text: 2 Weak and 2 Vulnerable is well worth 1 energy in almost any deck!

SEVERANCE.text: Decent damage paired with a bunch of card draw and Soul synergies. Keep in mind that you don't HAVE to play Souls the turn you draw them; if you've already spent 2 Energy on this and don't have much left to use this turn, maybe discard the Soul you generated to draw later.

BANSHEES_CRY.text: Obviously not a great card unless you have Ethereal cards in your deck, but if you do this is worth grabbing. It's particularly strong against multiple enemies, but even in single enemy fights, dealing 33 or more damage for 1 or 0 is very worthwhile.

DEVOUR_LIFE.text: Pushes decks with lots of souls over the top, allowing them to easily survive any enemy in the game.

MISERY.text: Misery has a limited upper bound because it doesn't do much in fights with single enemies in them, but it can often do some very impressive things in multi-enemy fights. Watch out for fights where enemies have their own debuffs which you can spread to the other enemies in the fight.

OBLIVION.text: Even without synergies, Oblivion is a passable card. It shines when paired with payoffs for applying Debuffs or Doom, or with ways to spam lots of cards in a turn (like Souls).

SEANCE.text: Solid Soul and Ethereal Synergy piece. Seance is one of Necrobinder's best cards for changing her deck composition during a fight, especially if you can get an upgraded copy of it.

SHARED_FATE.text: Permanent Strength reduction is very powerful. That said, 2 isn't a huge number, and some decks do feel the downside of the -2 Strength on Self downside.

UNDEATH.text: Can be tricky to use; don't flood your deck with copies of this to a point where it can't draw damage anymore. My favorite run with Undeath applied Retain to it, which meant I could hold a bunch of them in my hand to use whenever the other cards I drew weren't enough to Block that turn.

PROTECTOR.text: A bit better than Unleash, but not one of the better Ancient options for Necrobinder.

DEFILE.text: Good damage for 1 energy, and relevant synergy with Ethereal cards. Often worth taking during the "add some more damage to the deck" phase of Act 1.

FEAR.text: One of Necrobinder's decent damage commons. Works later with Debuff, Ethereal, and "big Attack" synergy spaces, which means it has lots of ways to retain value later in the run if you take it early on.

GRAVE_WARDEN.text: Decent Block amount + entry into the Soul synergy space. Not a bad card to pick up early, it's unusual for a deck to hate having one, even if all it's using Souls for is drawing a couple of cards.

GRAVEBLAST.text:
If your deck revolves heavily around a card you'd like to play multiple times, or a combination of cards you want to play together, Graveblast is a strong enabler.

Note that the upgrade both increases damage AND removes Exhaust.

NEGATIVE_PULSE.text: Negative Pulse can get very strong in the right sort of run; it does very well with other cards which reward you for applying Debuffs or specifically Doom. However, early on in the game it can be quite awkward, as it doesn't block for enough to be a strong Block card and its damage lines up poorly against quite a few enemy mechanics in the first two Acts of the game.

UNLEASH.text: Can be substantial damage in fights where you manage to get Osty's health high and keep it high. Pay attention for turns where you could play a Summon card to increase Osty's health before you play this to deal extra damage.

WISP.text: If your deck could beneficially spend extra energy per turn, grab a Wisp! Keep in mind that Necrobinder has several other options for energy gain though, so don't overdo it on Wisps if you can afford to wait a bit and find better options.

BURY.text: Enough damage that it's worth going out of your way to try to be able to play it, but it's hard to get around the fact that you only have 3 Energy per turn in Act 1 and this costs more than that. Still potentially worth trying to make work with some energy gain though!

DREDGE.text: Excellent for setting up ideal turns in longer fights. Good upgrade. A bit slow to take right at the start of the run.

HAUNT.text: Reliable way to increase damage in a deck which plays lots of Souls, but a more convenient way to achieve that might be to just play the good damage cards you already took earlier in the run when you draw them with the Souls you're playing.

MELANCHOLY.text: Keep in mind that Osty's deaths count for Melancholy, so if you're clever about having Osty die while taking little damage yourself you can have Melancholy costing 0 fairly quickly in fights. As such, it can be a good Block card in a deck which needs extra help in longer fights.

PAGESTORM.text: A good support card for decks built around Ethereal cards, especially if you can find an upgraded one.

VEILPIERCER.text: Passable damage, but most exciting for the ability to discount Ethereal cards. Has a specifically noteworthy synergy with Sculpting Strike, which can make a 3+ Cost card Ethereal to discount it to 0.

CALL_OF_THE_VOID.text: Decent enabler for Ethereal synergies, as well as just giving you an extra card to choose from per turn. However, Call of the Void is very slow, unreliable, and doesn't actually increase the output of your deck very much by itself unless it's supporting something else.

REANIMATE.text: A good chunk of defense which will persist between turns, but 3 Energy is an inefficient price, so it's okay to pass on this if you're short on Energy and don't have a way to cheat it into play.

REAPER_FORM.text: Extremely powerful if you can get it into play and have big Attacks, but not worth speculating on if your deck doesn't have the ability to support it. Probably the best way to get value from Reaper Form is to generate it off a Power Potion (18% chance), in which case it'll cost 0 without you needing to do any work.

SPIRIT_OF_ASH.text: Nice Support card for decks with a good number of Ethereal cards. If I'm getting at least 4 Block per turn out of this I'm already happy about having it.

SQUEEZE.text: Cloning this is a hilarious way to win. Very high damage attack even in some decks which aren't focusing on Osty attacks but have a couple of them incidentally.

BODYGUARD.text:
Bodyguard is often comparable to a Defend, but has a lot of small interactions with Osty to look out for. For example, you can sacrifice Osty with another card, then play Bodyguard to resummon him to play more Osty attacks on the same turn.

Also keep in mind that you can effectively use this to store up "Block" for later turns.

Which damage is blocked by Osty and which isn't is a bit complex and finnicky. For example: Osty won't block burns from hurting you at end of turn.

DRAIN_POWER.text: 10 Damage for 1 isn't awful, but the upgrading in Discard effect is very slow to reap benefits and will even be entirely irrelevant in some runs.

FLATTEN.text:
Damage Commons desperately need to be reliable. Drawing this on a turn where you can't discount it when you could have taken a reliably 1-Cost card which dealt as much damage as it can lose your entire runs.

That said, if it's the best you're offered, you do have to take some Damage Commons usually.

POKE.text: Not an awful way to deal damage early on, but will increasingly feel like you've added a low-impact nothing card to your deck as the run progresses.

REAP.text:
Not incredible damage per energy ratio, but putting it only a 3-Cost card with Retain ensures that you can hit enemies decently well on turns where they don't attack you, and Necrobinder has some synergies with high-cost Cards and high-damage Attacks.

Sometimes okay to grab for Act 1 damage.

REAVE.text: Inoffensive early game damage card which opens up some Soul Synergy potential later in the run. Not my favorite Act 1 Damage Common because it deals relatively little damage compared to others, but I'll take it sometimes.

SCULPTING_STRIKE.text: Sculpting Strike offers you the ability to modify your deck over the course of a longer combat. You can make cards Ethereal and not play them, letting them exhaust, or play them and benefit from Ethereal Synergies. Unfortunately, it deals relatively little damage, and its synergistic effects are extremely slow to actually deploy in a fight.

CLEANSE.text: In theory Cleanse can be used to remove chaff from your deck over time in order to end up with a powerful combo of cards toward the end of the fight, but in practice many fights are too threatening for this to be appealing to most decks.

COUNTDOWN.text: Passable damage per turn, especially for Boss Fights, but perhaps most useful because it guarantees that you're applying Doom every turn, which is valuable for Death's Door, one of the characters best Block cards.

DEATH_MARCH.text: Cards which give you payoff specifically for drawing extra cards in a turn are usually not very impressive because drawing extra cards in a turn is already strong by itself, and Death March doesn't have good output by itself without that sort of support.

HIGH_FIVE.text: High Five is a bit too expensive for its effect. It's hard to spend two energy in a turn on damage sometimes, and it asks you to then spend even more energy than that to take advantage of the Vulnerable you've applied.

RIGHT_HAND_HAND.text: A little extra damage for any deck with 2-Cost cards, but difficult to get much more out of than that.

SPUR.text: Passable Block card, and nice to have retain on defensive cards sometimes! I don't take it unless it's common for me to have Osty survive incoming damage in fights though.

HANG.text: Usually a bit slow, but if your deck can recur this somehow, or gets more than one of them, it scales extremely quickly.

SENTRY_MODE.text: Slow but effective Ethereal scaling option. I don't take this unless I really want some extra Ethereal cards for some reason, but sometimes I do!

SOUL_STORM.text: Okay damage option for a deck with lots of Souls, but not usually the best one, and not impressive unless you already have Souls working.

THE_SCYTHE.text: Can be pickable up until the end of Act 1, but it will make you weaker for a while while you try to scale it up. Keep in mind that there are ways to enhance a big attack's output with support cards, and Necrobinder has a few quite good ones.

TIMES_UP.text: Retain on Upgrade is a great improvement to the card, if you're able to get it upgraded. Time's Up is an okay way to halve the length of longer fights if most of your damage comes from Doom, but will often be awkward or worse in other parts of the run.

FORBIDDEN_GRIMOIRE.text: Many Necrobinder decks benefit from their commons throughout the entire run, and some fights reward you for having a decently-sized deck, so Forbidden Grimoire can have limited upside, especially if you're already removing your Strikes at Stores and Events.

STRIKE_NECROBINDER.text: Necrobinder's Strikes are already quite bad just in her Starter Deck, as Unleash rewards blocking every turn with extra damage. Later she has a couple of appealing cards which reduce her Strength, making them even worse.

DEFEND_NECROBINDER.text: Necrobinder isn't excited to play Defend later in the game, but they'll do in a pinch.

AFTERLIFE.text: Summoning can work to store up HP for later turns, but the most threatening fights in the game tend to attack you every turn, in which case this is just an unimpressive Defend which doesn't scale with Dexterity.

SOW.text: I haven't found Area of Effect damage to be important enough to take mediocre AoE Damage Cards over single-target alternatives, and Sow is a very poor card in any fight without multiple enemies in it.

CALCIFY.text: Even in a deck with several Osty Attacks I'd rather have 1. A different deck but also 2. Another good Osty Attack than this.

RATTLE.text: Barely better than an Attack Common in situations where you DO draw it with another Osty Attack, and terrible in situations where you don't.

SHROUD.text: Doom tends to be applied in large amounts, so the amount of Block you're getting per Doom applied from this card is quite low. Every now and then you're in a run where you're applying lots of small amounts of Doom repeatedly, either to enemies or sometimes yourself, and Shroud can make a lot of Block for you.

SIC_EM.text: Often worse than a Strike. If you end up with several copies of Fetch in your deck this can do quite well, but in most decks it's not pickable.

EIDOLON.text: 1) It costs 2 energy for this card to do nothing, an awful lots of the time. 2) I am honor-bound to negatively review any card which gives the player Intangible, as it is dishonorable to not let the enemy hit you.

NECRO_MASTERY.text: Awkward and slow way to deal some area of effect damage. Not usually worth trying to make work.

SACRIFICE.text: Very awkward Block card. Notably, this essentially can't be used to Block well in fights where you're being attacked for more than you're able to defend for without it. It's at its best in fights where you're only attacked every other turn, or something like that, but in general I don't think you need to bother trying to work out how to get good value out of it.

CLAW.text: The formula for winning with Claw is quite simple: Block with Relics or good Block cards while drawing through your deck for lots of Claws. All For One or Feral often win the run easily from there, but Claws can win even without them. Remember that a deck with 3+ Claws often would prefer card draw or block over another copy of Claw.

FERAL.text: Extremely powerful engine/payoff card for decks with 0-Cost Attacks. Doesn't have to be paired with Claw, although that is the most obvious way to make it strong. I like it with FTL quite a lot to draw extra cards and deal a little extra damage, for example. The interaction with Potions or Relics which generate 0-Cost Attacks can be quite nice as well, as you'll get the chance to play them again, although they're usually only discounted the first time they're played.

GLACIER.text: This is usually the best possible way for Defect to make enough Block to survive the game.

COOLHEADED.text: Perfect support card for almost all of Defect's offensive strategies. Draw toward your damage while creating a very good amount of Block per Energy spent. A Frost Orb will often make 10+ Block after being channeled.

OVERCLOCK.text: Putting Burns in your Discard Pile doesn't have much drawback until much later in the fight, and Statuses can even potentially have upside for Defect, so this card is extremely strong and often worth upgrading.

ALL_FOR_ONE.text: Defect has a lot of strong 0-Cost cards and All for One is the best way to take them from good to great.

BUFFER.text: Buffer is a very high priority upgrade. Once upgraded, it often lets you spend a lot of Energy on Scaling or Damaging enemies. Especially good in Boss Fights and many single-enemy Elite Fights.

MODDED.text: Gaining Orb Slots for little-to-no cost is great! Usually hoping to play this twice in longer fights.

SUPERCRITICAL.text: Four Energy is a LOT of Energy. Pair this with Card Draw and put together an awesome turn, essentially no matter what you're doing, or combine it with some big Energy combo like Multi-Cast + Dark Orb to instantly end a fight. It's possible to not want this yet in Act 1, but it'll often be very exciting later on in the run.

BIASED_COGNITION.text: Biased Cognition requires a little bit of user skill. If you're building decks which kill slower than they could, the punishment from losing one Focus per turn can start to stack up. That said, the better you get, the better it gets, and one of the ways to get better is to start picking it! When used well It's probably the best card in Defect's entire card pool.

QUADCAST.text: Great output for 1 Energy. Tons of Block with a Frost Orb, tons of damage with a damage Orb. Hard to go wrong here.

HELIX_DRILL.text: Excellent damage for 0-Cost, and scales with all sorts of different ways to truly break it.

GO_FOR_THE_EYES.text: Defect's best way to apply Weak, and fits into its best synergy package (0-Cost cards).

BEAM_CELL.text: I'm happy to have a Beam Cell in an attack-damage based run, ideally upgraded, and I find that most of my runs aim to Block with Frost Orbs while dealing damage with Attacks, so it's usually a card I'm very happy to be taking at least one of.

FTL.text: The default is to pick FTL when you see it, but do watch out for occasional downsides. It's not at its best in decks with lots of other card draw, as you may not draw it until it has stopped working for the turn. Both the Queen and Doormaker have elements to their Boss Fight at the end of Act 3 which make it less valuable in those fights, too.

BOOST_AWAY.text: 6 Block for 0 is fine on Defect, but Boost Away is most exciting because it offers potential synergies with Statuses or All For One. I typically take one of these if it's offered in Act 1, and may add more if they turn out to be particularly good this run.

ROCKET_PUNCH.text: Run-winning as long as you have a couple of cards which generate statuses. Extremely good upgrade, extremely good in multiples, and extremely good with Feral and All For One.

BOOT_SEQUENCE.text: Boot Sequence saves a LOT of health in decks lacking good Relics to help with Turn 1, but can feel like a dead card if you do have a strong Turn 1 already. It's made a bit better by Hologram, which can let you get it back on later turns if it isn't used on Turn 1.

HOLOGRAM.text: Hologram keeps getting better and better as the run goes on, as the card it gets back is stronger and stronger. Don't overdo it with too many copies early, but most Defect decks are happy to have a couple of these, and some happily take even more.

SKIM.text:
The stronger your deck gets, the stronger Skim gets. It draws your broken combos faster, but isn't very useful if you don't have any of those.

I'm usually hoping to start being excited about taking Skims sometime in Act 2, but am not always prioritizing picking it in Act 1.

BALL_LIGHTNING.text: Defect's best pure damage common for Act 1. Lots of damage, very little in the way of requirements for support. Can become awkward later, as Lightning Orbs don't synergize with many of Defect's stronger strategies.

COLD_SNAP.text: Strong "both ways" common for Act 1, but you don't WANT to be relying on it for Frost Orb generation later in the run, as there are stronger options. That said, if it's the best you're offered, you may have to try to make do with it.

CHILL.text: A very nice way to make Frost Orbs, and the Upgrade to remove Exhaust can make sense in decks with ways to play it multiple times.

GENETIC_ALGORITHM.text: Genetic Algorithm rapidly reaches a point where it's fully Blocking on almost every turn it's played on, and can be worth Duplicating or removing Exhaust from if you get the chance to do either of those things. Unfortunately it's unlikely to be found early in the run, and finding it later than the first half of Act 2 makes it quite unappealing.

ICE_LANCE.text: Probably the third best way to make Frost Orbs available to the character. Decent pick up, and there are a variety of ways to increase its output using enchantments, potions, or other cards, which can make it especially good.

MACHINE_LEARNING.text: One of Defect's issues is that all of its strategies require drawing combinations of cards. Orbs need generators + focus, Status synergies need the generators + payoffs + drawing through the Statuses, and 0-Cost stuff needs to draw lots of 0-Cost stuff. Machine Learning tends to help out most Defect decks quite a lot, and can be a nice upgrade for decks with safe Turn 1's.

METEOR_STRIKE.text:
You need to be a little clever to get a Meteor Strike played, but once you have the extra output from 3 Plasma Orbs will often win you the fight easily. Note that Plasma Orbs Evoke for 2 each, so if you can play this and Evoke the Orbs immediately it's actually Energy positive already!

This is a degenerate combo card which you'll find more success with the more you practice with it.

REBOOT.text:
Reboot has obvious upside: draw a bunch of extra cards.

Be aware of its downside: reshuffling your deck might make it harder to find your best Powers, or might fill your new draw pile with Statuses earlier than necessary.

That said, it's still usually worth taking this card.

TRASH_TO_TREASURE.text: Tons of output for any deck which generates its own statuses. Channeling multiple random Orbs per turn adds up very quickly. I don't personally think this is worth speculating on if you don't have the appropriate support cards in your deck yet, though.

DEFRAGMENT.text: Important Upgrade. When evaluating Defragment, keep in mind that it increases how much Orbs Evoke for as well as their Passive Output. For example, playing Glacier with 3 Frost Orbs already channeled results in a Defragment+ generating an additional 10 Block that turn.

COMPACT.text: Can be worth picking up for some runs where you are weak to a status-generating Boss or Elite fight, but Compact struggles a little with the fact that Statuses usually go to your Discard pile, and once you're through your Draw pile the first time the fight is often essentially over already.

TESLA_COIL.text: Excellent 0-Cost damage, but requires you to have Lightning Orbs, so less easy to use than other 0-Cost options.

BARRAGE.text: Solid damage. My most successful Defect decks tend to use Frost orbs quite a lot, which means they could use a way to turn full orb slots into actually ending the fight, and Barrage is a good way to achieve that.

FOCUSED_STRIKE.text: Okay damage, but there are better damage commons, and Focused Strike suffers from being at its best in decks which are already good anyway. If you can channel a bunch of orbs and still need a damage common it can make sense, but if your deck is already doing that why do you need more damage commons?

GUNK_UP.text: 12 Targeted Damage for 1 is a decent but not incredible equation. The Slime added to Discard can work with some Status Synergies, but I haven't found them to be the strongest thing to do on the character.

LEAP.text: Perfectly passable Block common. You don't want to have to rely on Leaps to survive, but if you don't have better options yet and need a Block card this one is fine.

LIGHTNING_ROD.text: Lightning Rod is a confusing card; it deals damage very slowly and Blocks a bit to keep you alive while that damage comes into play, but the Lightning Orbs it creates are unreliable and push better Orbs out of your bar. It's okay to take one early just because of its high potential for output, but don't overcommit to them.

TURBO.text: Great enabler for strategies which care about lots of energy, but Defect is probably the best character at winning while spending extremely little energy, so don't assume that you'll want it by default in any run.

BULK_UP.text: Never underestimate the value of +Dexterity in longer fights in this game. That said, Defect often Blocks using Orbs, which are actually hurt by this card, and many of its ways to deal damage are also ambivalent about extra Strength, so this card is only useful situationally in runs where you haven't found better solutions to scaling.

CAPACITOR.text: Orb Scaling is quite awkward in Slay the Spire 2; it's hard to find Focus to enhance them. It can sometimes do well enough, and Capacitor will be a key component of runs where it does, but this is the sort of card I don't take unless I'm somewhat down that path already.

FIGHT_THROUGH.text: Great Block Output per Energy, but Two Wounds is painful enough to feel like a real drawback even on Defect with your potential status synergies. Nice pickup in a large deck with Block requirements, or if you have enough Status payoffs.

ITERATION.text: Great payoff card for Status Synergies, but also often good just against enemies who put some Statuses in your deck on their own. It tends to make its way into my deck if the Act Boss gives statuses and I'm worried about not having enough card draw for the fight, for example.

SHADOW_SHIELD.text: Don't overestimate this card; the Dark Orb represents very slow damage, and you don't want to have to wait a long time to close out many of the fights in the game. It Blocks for a good amount and that's a valuable thing to have access to, but this is just a solid Block card, not an auto-pick.

SMOKESTACK.text: Smokestack provides enough payoff to be worth picking in a deck with Status generation, but not enough to take it in a deck which doesn't have any of that yet in the hopes it will become good later.

COOLANT.text: Solid Passive Block generation. Best in decks with a Capacitor and varied Orb types, but okay to play just for 4 Block per Turn if that's all you're getting out of it. More valuable for longer fights, so don't take it if you're struggling against the fast fights.

ECHO_FORM.text: Echo Form has an extremely powerful effect, but it's very hard to put it into play. It's best in decks which need a super Power to win the Boss Gauntlet and can survive essentially having a blank card in them for the shorter fights.

MULTI_CAST.text: Multi-Cast is the de facto payoff card for decks which can make tons of Energy somehow. It can be paired best with a Plasma Orb to double your Energy, or a Dark Orb to kill many enemies outright. Evoking a Frost Orb multiple times can do fine to survive a turn as well.

SHATTER.text: Defect's best Area of Effect damage card, and a nice enabler for strategies using Dark Orbs which don't have much ability to evoke them quickly. I'm probably not taking this card in Act 2 or 3, but it's good enough to make it into my deck in Act 1, and sometimes has use later on as well.

SIGNAL_BOOST.text: Heavily dependent on the quality of your Powers. If you have an awesome Rare Power to play an additional time with this it'll likely do great, but if you don't it's not worth speculating on.

DUALCAST.text:
Decent Output which improves as the run goes on and your Orb variety increases (and maybe you find some Focus!).

It's often worth Dualcasting a Lightning Orb instead of playing a Strike in early fights, look out for that and don't be afraid to do a little math to work out which option deals better damage for the situation you're in.

LOOP.text: Loop has low but consistent output. It's unfortunate that it doesn't combo well with temporary Focus, but it does enough with a Frost Orb (or perhaps Dark Orb if you're in a run using those) to be worth picking up, and it's an especially valuable upgrade, so I'm more likely to take it if I have a campfire coming up and no cards I really want to upgrade yet.

CHARGE_BATTERY.text: Passable block common, but Defect's card pool has a lot of zero-costs, so energy isn't all that important in a lot of its runs. Skipping by default unless there's a compelling reason to care about generating some extra energy.

COMPILE_DRIVER.text: Energy generation is fairly low, as are the payoffs for channeling different types of Orbs, so Compile Driver doesn't feel like it has much of a place in this game.

HOTFIX.text: Does almost nothing unless you're already in a commanding position in the fight. Cards which help you when you're weak are a lot more exciting than cards which give you even more payoff once you already have a bunch of orbs set up.

UPROAR.text:
There is absolutely a strategy which wants this card. You need to remove Strikes heavily and pick up some high-impact attacks while avoiding the low-impact 0-cost ones.

Unfortunately that doesn't match up well with Defect's overall card pool, so I wouldn't typically pick this up in Act 1, and once I'm in Act 2 I usually have too many low-cost attacks to justify it.

DARKNESS.text: Can be good for Boss-fight damage or some Elites, but waiting multiple turns for your damage and then still needing to line it up with a Dualcast or Multicast to get really good value out of it is very awkward. I'm hoping not to have to use Dark Orbs in my runs, but if I do it'd be because my deck's damage was too low going into a long fight.

DOUBLE_ENERGY.text: This is an extremely breakable card, but isn't easy to pick in Act 1. It pairs surprisingly well with Unceasing Top, which is unfortunately a singular Relic you're unlikely to see. Failing that, it fits nicely into some decks with excess card draw or particularly high energy costs.

GLASSWORK.text: Decent output, 5 Block and somewhere in the range of 4-12 area of effect damage usually. Unfortunately it's a bit too slow and its values are a bit too low to keep up with most of the game's tougher fights, so I'm usually skipping it.

NULL.text: Null is a very inoffensive card which unfortunately doesn't do very much. Like, it does three things which aren't very good at the same time. Paying attention to factors which could make any of its parts better than usual, like excess energy, desperate need for Weak, or desperate need for Scaling damage, could give you reasons to take it, but by default I'm skipping this.

REFRACT.text: There are some fights that Refract does INCREDIBLY well in, but they don't tend to be the toughest fights in the game, and spending 3 Energy on a card which only deals damage will almost certainly result in your taking a substantial hit in return. I don't hate taking one, but my better decks don't.

STORM.text: Unfortunately, Defect's powers have very split identities in this game, so it's hard to make a deck which focuses around taking lots of them. Storm is more likely to fit into a deck which gets a lot of Focus somehow, and something like Biased Cognition or Echo Form to massively increase its output. In runs like that, it can potentially serve as enough damage to win lategame.

SUNDER.text:
Not typically a very strong card, but having a 3-Cost Attack can have some value sometimes. It gives you something to pair with a Potion or Relic which increases Attack Damage, for example, or something to Enchant with Slither, which can randomize its cost when drawn.

I take one of these in Act 1 sometimes, and am not upset if I transform into one.

SYNCHRONIZE.text: Big payoff card for Orb strategies, but needs a lot of other things to fall into place before it's worth taking. I'd want at least a Capacitor and three different Orb Slots before I was interested in it.

TEMPEST.text: Tempest is a relevant payoff for some Energy-generation strategies Defect has available. It's possible sometimes to set things up so you're playing Double Energy multiple times, or storing Energy with Ice Cream. In runs like that, Tempest can provide enough damage for lategame. Most of the time I wouldn't recommend taking it, though.

THUNDER.text: Can be okay damage scaling for longer fights in Act 1 or 2, but doesn't really scale with much in a way to make it exciting in Act 3.

WHITE_NOISE.text: It's fine to take a White Noise any time your deck could use a little more scaling for longer fights, but don't expect it to be a great card unless you have some other Cards or Relics which make Powers particularly good for you.

ADAPTIVE_STRIKE.text: 0-Cost 18 Damage Attacks are great, but the upfront cost on this card is too high for it to be appealing for anything other than very long fights, and even in those it's reliant on you drawing it before your first reshuffle or else you likely die before it deals any relevant damage.

CONSUMING_SHADOW.text: Consuming Shadow often puts you in a "stuck" state with Orbs where your middle Orbs are Dark Orbs which have scaled lots of damage, but you're always wanting to channel another Orb every turn, and that one gets Evoked by Consuming Shadow, leading to them never making it to the right or left of your Orb Slots to be Evoked. Make sure you have a solution to that if you're taking this card, which is a passable damage card as long as you do!

HYPERBEAM.text: Okay damage, and can be worth picking up for specific multi-enemy fights if they are troubling for your deck, but losing Focus is a huge downside given that Defect's main unique mechanic is Orbs which are likely to be made entirely useless by such a debuff.

RAINBOW.text: Rainbow is flexible enough that there are lots of reasons it might be good, but its raw numbers aren't such that it's guaranteed to always be good. Anything which benefits from varied orbs makes it better. Any specific reasons to care about the orbs it channels make it better. The fact that it exhausts might be useful if you're hoping to play a smaller deck built around a few specific cards later in the run. Lots to think about for a fairly straight-forward card.

SPINNER.text: Deals decent damage for longer fights, but monopolizes your Orb Slots with negatively-scaling damage Orbs. I've found this useful in quite a few runs, but make sure you have some good Block cards to stay alive long enough for it to do anything if you take it.

ZAP.text: Decent damage card for Act 1, but there isn't much value to channeling a Lightning Orb other than that unfortunately.

FLAK_CANNON.text: The number on Flak Cannon feels substantially too low to be exciting. It's a very bad card unless your deck creates a huge number of statuses or you're fighting an enemy which does. Fortunately for Flak Cannon, one of the Act 3 Bosses fits that bill, so it'll be worth picking up in situations where you're weak to that fight, but otherwise I'd recommend passing on it.

MOMENTUM_STRIKE.text: Unusual for me to want this. Defect has several better 0-Cost cards which start out costing 0 already without needing any energy investment.

SWEEPING_BEAM.text: Very rare that I want this. Area of Effect damage isn't much more valuable than Single-Target damage, and the number here is quite low.

CHAOS.text: Could be okay if you were in a run with some Focus, Compile Drivers, and Orb Slots, but that's a lot of things which are unlikely to happen in a row.

FUSION.text: Fusion's main use case is in a deck which wants to do some fancy Double Energy or Multi-Cast combos and needs a Plasma Orb to set them up. The rest of the time this is a very slow Energy gain card on a character that doesn't need one.

HAILSTORM.text: Fun to set up Frost Orbs and watch the enemies die to your Hailstorm, but this card is a bit too conditional, slow, and has no real payoff potential; it doesn't scale to be stronger with anything else you can do really.

SCAVENGE.text: Can be used to protect against bad Statuses, to set up for slow infinites, or to set up for big turns, but mostly this card is just slow and doesn't do very much.

SCRAPE.text: The issue with Scrape is that even decks which care heavily about 0-Cost cards have some very important 1+ Cost cards they need to draw and play. It can fit into a deck with multiple 0-Costs and do okay, but even in the perfect situation for it it's still overshadowed by other options.

SUBROUTINE.text: It's unusual to build a Defect deck which wants to take tons of powers, and the ones worth taking are usually worth paying their Energy cost for anyway. Subroutine fits into some runs with (very specifically) Game Piece, which makes Powers draw a card when played, but it's unusual for me to want it anywhere else.

SYNTHESIS.text: Very little reason to take this unless you have an important 3-Cost Power and don't mind having an extra Attack card in your deck.

CREATIVE_AI.text: VERY slow scaling, can be an okay option for a Boss fight, but honestly it's a little slow even for those. You usually need strong Power Synergies for this to be an appealing card, and even then it isn't all that good.

VOLTAIC.text: If you can play this 4 times it's very easy to kill any enemy in the game with it. That said, it's very difficult to play a 3-Cost card which only deals damage more than one time in a fight. Fits into some more defensive decks as a scaling option for Boss Fights, or some very aggressive decks which already make a lot of Lightning, but doesn't have a place in most decks Defect can build.

DEFEND_DEFECT.text: Blocking is important, but Defect doesn't have anything in particular which is likely to make its Defends stronger over the course of the run.

STRIKE_DEFECT.text: Defect's Starter Deck has 6 cards which deal damage and 4 Defends, leading to taking a lot of damage on turns where it can't Block enough early in the run. Removing Strikes early is a good way to address this quickly.
